title: Dynamic Focus Windows and Snapshot-Driven Scope Trimming for Cycle Capacity
creator: Amaya Patel
description:
Background: As cycles compress and multiple initiatives compete for limited engineering capacity, ad-hoc scope cuts and late reassignments cause churn and missed targets. Existing cycle playbooks emphasize pre-cycle tradeoffs but offer limited tooling for mid-cycle, evidence-driven scope decisions.

Proposal summary: Introduce a lightweight operational pattern — Dynamic Focus Windows — paired with a Snapshot-Driven Scope Trimming process. Dynamic Focus Windows are short, named intervals (48–72 hours) where product and Eng align on a narrow set of outcomes and temporarily deprioritize non-critical work. Snapshot-Driven Scope Trimming uses an immutable snapshot of deliverable status (progress %, blocking issues, owner availability, test/regression risk) to run rapid, auditable scope decisions with minimal meetings.

Goals: reduce mid-cycle churn, improve predictability of committed deliverables, and create an auditable trail for scope decisions tied to data. This should lower rework by ~15% and reduce emergency reassignments by ~25% in initial pilots.

Key components: 1) Focus Window taxonomy (Urgent Finish, Quality Stabilize, Dependency Unblock) with explicit guardrails; 2) Snapshot tooling template (Google Sheet + embedded query to cycle velocity dashboard) that captures progress and risk signals at snapshot time; 3) Decision rubric and voting matrix (PM, Eng lead, Design lead, Eng manager) that yields 1 of: keep, postpone, handoff, or reduce scope; 4) Swapboard protocol to enable short-term staff swaps across teams for urgent finish windows; 5) Roll-forward notes (what was trimmed and how to reintroduce later).

Why different from current playbooks: Rather than continuously renegotiating scope, this process time-boxes decisions to short windows anchored on a data snapshot. That reduces subjective debates and creates consistent, repeatable artifacts for post-cycle retros and OKR adjustments.

Deliverables: playbook doc (Confluence), snapshot template (Drive), swapboard runbook, pilot checklist, and retrospective dashboard queries.

Open questions:
- Which metrics should be mandatory in a snapshot (progress %, test pass rate, unblock count)?
- What guardrails for using a Focus Window (max 2 per team per cycle)?
- Should swapboard transfers be compensated with capacity credits in future cycles?
acceptance_criteria: Confluence playbook published with concrete step-by-step process and examples
Snapshot template available and wired to cycle velocity dashboard queries
Pilot executed across 2 product initiatives and one platform team in Cycle 2025-W10/W11
Swapboard runbook validated with at least one successful short-term staff swap and manager approval recorded
Retrospective shows measurable reduction in late reassignments for pilot teams (target: 15% reduction)
success_metrics: Percent reduction in emergency reassignments (target 25% for pilot teams)
Decrease in mid-cycle unplanned scope churn (target 15%)
Time from Focus Window start to decision (target < 48 hours)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (week 0–2): finalize playbook and templates; get approvals from Eng leadership and Design; instrument dashboard queries. Phase 2 (week 3–4): pilot with 3 teams (2 product + 1 platform). Phase 3 (week 5): collect retrospective data and refine rubric. Phase 4 (week 6): broaden to additional teams and add swapboard automation in Console if helpful.
engineering_notes: ENG must expose per-PR and per-branch status tags to snapshot via dashboard query (ENG-22011).
Swapboard requires manager opt-in and a simple override API for short-lived assignments; initial pilot can use manual handoffs.
Automated snapshot export should be read-only and timestamped to ensure auditability.
design_notes: Create a compact visual template for snapshot that highlights friction points (blocked work, flaky tests, infra incidents).
Design lead to create micro-UX for swapboard confirmations (email + Slack + Console flag).
